result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A labels every bar with its exact dollar value, uses a light green emphasis on May that makes the peak obvious, and has a plain light look that suits a garden newsletter. Its one rendering flaw is that the Dec bar is narrower than the others, and it adds a short caption that wasn't asked for. B is clean and honest, with gridlines and one bar color, but its dark card styling, full-year total and 'View as table' toggle go beyond 'nothing fancy', and most values have to be read off the axis. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B labels every bar with its exact dollar value, says plainly that the figures are US dollars for 2025, and makes May stand out with one darker bar. Its flaws are that the December bar is narrower than the others, the axis ticks are odd ($16k/$32k), and the footnote is a little wordy. A is clean and honest, but readers must estimate most values from the gridlines, and its dark card plus 'View as table' toggle suit a newsletter less well.
